pull.title: test: look for the wtxid in p2p_blocksonly
pull.body:
In `blocks_relay_conn_tests`, the check that a transaction submitted over RPC is not announced to a block-relay-only peer looks for its txid among the peer's invs. The peer is a `P2PTxInvStore`, which negotiates wtxidrelay, so an announcement would carry the wtxid. The MiniWallet transaction has a witness, so its txid and wtxid differ, and the check passes whether or not the node announces it.

This checks the wtxid instead. To see the difference, open that connection as `outbound-full-relay`: the old check still passes, the new one fails. It also adds an `outbound-full-relay` peer that must receive the wtxid announcement first, so the check cannot pass silently again.

#35920 also edits `blocks_relay_conn_tests`; the two do not conflict.

Found while porting these tests to https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-node-tests.

test: look for the wtxid in p2p_blocksonly

The connection that checks a transaction submitted over RPC is not
announced to a block-relay-only peer uses P2PTxInvStore, which negotiates
wtxidrelay. The node would therefore announce the transaction by its
wtxid, and the assertion looked for the txid, which cannot be in the
store for a transaction carrying a witness: it passed whether or not the
transaction was announced.

Assert on the wtxid instead. With the connection opened as
outbound-full-relay rather than block-relay-only, the old assertion still
passes and the new one fails.

Also open an outbound-full-relay connection and assert that the wtxid
was announced on it. The two assertions differ only by `not`, so if the
announcement or its id changes, the test fails instead of the absence
check passing silently.

ACK 22535b460568be47e57aadfbe50d489becb77577

Ran p2p_blocksonly.py with v1 and v2 transport. With conn changed to outbound-full-relay, the new assertion fails while the old txid check still passes. Using txid in both assertions also fails at the positive control.

comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -112,7 +112,8 @@ def blocks_relay_conn_tests(self):
         self.nodes[0].setmocktime(int(time.time()) + 60)
 
         conn.sync_with_ping()
-        assert int(txid, 16) not in conn.get_invs()
+        # The peer negotiated wtxidrelay, so an announcement would carry the wtxid
+        assert int(wtxid, 16) not in conn.get_invs()
comments.body: maybe there should be another peer to check it is received for it? Otherwise the test will likely silently break again in the future?

comments.body: Done in c765571. I added an outbound-full-relay peer that must receive the wtxid announcement before the block-relay-only peer is checked, so the test fails if the node stops announcing the transaction or announces it under another id.

comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -105,14 +105,17 @@ def blocks_relay_conn_tests(self):
 
         self.log.info("Check that txs from RPC are not sent to blockrelay connection")
         conn = self.nodes[0].add_outbound_p2p_connection(P2PTxInvStore(), p2p_idx=1, connection_type="block-relay-only")
+        tx_relay_peer = self.nodes[0].add_outbound_p2p_connection(P2PTxInvStore(), p2p_idx=2, connection_type="outbound-full-relay")
 
         self.nodes[0].sendrawtransaction(tx_hex)
 
         # Bump time forward to ensure m_next_inv_send_time timer pops
         self.nodes[0].setmocktime(int(time.time()) + 60)
 
+        tx_relay_peer.wait_for_broadcast([wtxid])
comments.body:
There is no need to wait for a broadcast, when not using the unbroadcast set for this test. Also, with mocktime, this should probably be a sync_with_ping instead?

Finally, the point was that the test has the relevant assert directly inside, so that it is somewhat "self-checking". So the difference between the two asserts is just the `not`.
